---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Cash Yield on Knowledge Capital
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), 0.05), SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), TS_SUM(xrd, 5))), 0.5))
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms that have actually built a material knowledge stock, the priced characteristic is how much operating cash flow that stock throws off per dollar invested; high-yield research franchises are underpriced relative to research programs that consume capital without converting it into cash.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive shows funding-capacity conjunctions work but has not yet tested intangible *yield* successfully — the gen-0 trend version failed mainly because the yield was measured as a five-year slope on a degenerate denominator. Here the materiality indicator (R&D capital above 5% of assets) removes the small-R&D firms whose yield explodes, and the centered rank makes the extreme deciles high-yield versus low-yield researchers rather than researchers versus non-researchers, which is the structure that delivered fmb 4.45 in gen 1.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Worst-Year Total Liquidity Floor on Research
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(oancf, SUB(act, lct)), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: What protects a research program is total spendable resources in a bad year — operating cash flow plus net working capital — so the correct quality leg is a single worst-year resource floor rather than either the flow or the stock measured separately.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two strongest archived conjunctions used the cash-flow floor (alpha 4.2%, fmb 4.27) and net working capital (alpha 4.3%, ls_talpha 3.88 but fmb only 1.41), and their divergent Fama-MacBeth behavior suggests each captures part of the same resource constraint with different noise. Adding flow and stock inside one worst-year statistic — both already in assets-scaled units — is a single economic construct rather than a nested stack of two archived legs, and should sharpen the cross-sectional slope that the lumpier working-capital version lost.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Organic Minus Acquired Intangible Capital
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0))), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Not all intangible capital is equal: internally developed knowledge is expensed and unrecognized, while purchased goodwill is capitalized at deal prices that embed acquirer overpayment, so the organic-minus-acquired tilt of a firm's intangible base predicts returns once a cash-flow floor confirms the firm can sustain it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every archived intangibles leg so far measures intensity or composition versus tangible capital; none contrasts self-generated against purchased intangibles, which is where the accounting mispricing is concentrated. Netting five-year R&D against booked goodwill plus other intangibles produces one signed intangible-quality variable, and conjoining it with the validated worst-year cash-flow floor isolates firms whose unrecognized knowledge base is both large and financially supported.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Funded Research Ramp
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUB(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), revt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: An increase in research intensity is informative only in the context of the firm's ability to pay for it: cash-generative firms stepping up R&D are signalling opportunity, while cash-poor firms stepping up R&D are gambling and should underperform, so the same ramp earns opposite returns across funding states.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive tests intangible *levels* and floors extensively but not the change in intensity, and gen-0 evidence showed that funding-source conditioning (rather than a plain rank product) is what converts a change variable into a tradable spread. Centering the cash-flow leg makes the score sign-flip across funding states while firms with no change in research intensity sit near zero, giving a two-sided portfolio with a clear economic label on each side.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Research-Capitalized Earnings Floor
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: For intangible-intensive firms, reported ROA mismeasures both numerator and denominator; the economically meaningful durability test is the worst-year return on an intangible-augmented capital base with R&D added back to earnings, and research intensity is only credible when that adjusted floor is high.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This isolates one design choice against the gen-0 winner — replacing the raw cash-flow floor with a floor computed on a research-capitalized profitability definition — so a stronger result attributes the alpha to genuine intangible productivity rather than to a generic profitability screen, while a weaker one says the funding-flow interpretation is the right one. The adjusted ratio is well defined for all firms since the R&D add-back is zero for non-reporters, keeping coverage comparable to the archive's high-coverage signals.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Booked-Intangible Heaviness in Cash-Flow Drawdown
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at), 0.2), SUB(IND_RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), TS_MAX(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))), 0.5))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms carrying a heavy capitalized intangible and goodwill base face an impairment cliff that only bites when cash generation falls away from its own historical peak, so within the intangible-heavy population the cash-flow drawdown separates franchises whose book value is real from those facing writedowns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the first proposal to condition on booked intangible heaviness rather than research intensity, and it re-uses the drawdown construct that produced a positive but modest result in gen 1 in the population where it should matter most — firms whose balance sheet is more than 20% intangible. The centered rank yields a two-sided spread inside a single well-defined subpopulation, addressing the failure mode of the gen-0 goodwill signal whose strong cross-sectional slope did not translate into portfolio alpha.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Cash Yield on Knowledge Capital---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The materiality-indicator × centered-rank structure is a legitimate reuse of the archive's best-performing template applied to a genuinely new variable, but note the ranked quantity (operating cash flow per dollar of cumulative R&D) mechanically favors the *least* R&D-intensive firms within the material group and is heavily loaded on plain profitability, so it may test the opposite tilt from the "research franchise" story in the hypothesis.

---CRITIQUE Worst-Year Total Liquidity Floor on Research---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a mechanical merge of the two archived quality legs into one term that sums an annual flow (oancf) with a balance-sheet stock (act−lct) in incompatible units, and since net working capital is typically much larger it will be dominated by the already-tested working-capital version rather than constituting a distinct economic construct.

---CRITIQUE Organic Minus Acquired Intangible Capital---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The organic-versus-acquired intangible contrast is a genuinely new leg and the quality leg is held fixed for a clean one-change comparison, though the netted variable mixes two incompatible measurement bases (expensed cumulative R&D vs. deal-priced book intangibles) and risks being a repackaged bundle of the known R&D-to-assets and goodwill/acquisitiveness anomalies.

---CRITIQUE Funded Research Ramp---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Internally inconsistent — the R&D-change leg is an uncentered IND_RANK in [0,1], so the score's sign is determined entirely by the cash-flow rank and firms with no research-intensity change do *not* sit near zero as the reasoning claims, leaving a signal that is mostly a profitability sort scaled by ramp rank, with a huge tie mass at zero change for non-reporters.

---CRITIQUE Research-Capitalized Earnings Floor---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Economically well-motivated but this is the fourth instance of the same MIN(R&D-intensity, worst-year-profitability-floor) template in the archive (Weakest-Link, Margin Floor, Hidden Gap), so the R&D add-back and capitalized denominator amount to a cosmetic re-specification of an already-explored design rather than a substantively different mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Booked-Intangible Heaviness in Cash-Flow Drawdown---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Conditioning the drawdown construct on booked-intangible heaviness is a new and coherent subpopulation restriction with a clear impairment-cliff mechanism and a two-sided, well-labeled spread, though the drawdown leg is close to a profitability-deterioration proxy and the diagnostic value hinges on the 20% threshold not shrinking the effective sample too far.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Self-Funding Frequency Gate on Research
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), SUB(IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 0), 5)), 0.5))
HYPOTHESIS: Credibility comes from how *often* internal cash flow covered the research bill, not from the level of cash flow: a firm that paid for its own R&D in five years out of five has an institutionally financed program, while an equally research-intensive firm that covered it in one year out of five is running on external capital and should underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The gate counts years in which oancf exceeded R&D spending — a comparison of two same-unit annual flows, which repairs the flow-plus-stock unit incoherence the critic identified and produces a frequency statistic no archived signal contains. Centering the gate turns research intensity into a two-sided score, long consistently self-funded researchers and short chronically externally funded ones, the structure that produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes.
REASONING: Non-researchers receive near-zero weight from the intensity leg, so the spread is identified inside the population where the mechanism applies.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Double-Centered Research Ramp Interaction
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUB(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), SUB(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(xrd, revt), 1)), 0.5))
HYPOTHESIS: The pure interaction of funding capacity and research-intensity change is priced: cash-rich firms ramping R&D are exploiting real opportunities and cash-poor firms ramping R&D are gambling, while cash-poor firms cutting R&D are prudently retrenching and cash-rich firms cutting R&D are signalling exhausted opportunity sets.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Centering both legs removes each theme's main effect by construction, so the score is literally an interaction term with mean-zero legs and cannot be delivered by a profitability sort alone — the defect the critic identified in the uncentered version. Dropping COALESCE from the change leg confines the signal to genuine R&D reporters and eliminates the large tie mass of mechanical zero changes at non-reporting firms.
REASONING: All four quadrants carry an economically signed interpretation, which makes both the long and the short portfolios interpretable rather than residual.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Own-History Coincidence of Research and Cash Strength
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), 0.05), SUB(MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(xrd, revt), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)), 0.25))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable intangible productivity shows up as a within-firm state: a research-intensive firm that is simultaneously at the top of its own five-year range in research intensity *and* in cash generation is escalating investment out of demonstrated internal strength, whereas escalation from a firm-specific cash trough is a late-cycle stretch.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This abandons the cross-sectional MIN template entirely: both legs are TS_RANK positions inside the firm's own history, so firm-level profitability, size and industry are differenced out and the score cannot reload on the standard quality anomaly. Centering the product at 0.25 — the mean product of two independent within-firm uniforms — gives a two-sided spread inside the materially research-intensive population, and the joint-high requirement is a genuine timing interaction rather than a re-scaled level comparison.
